passage: In Class 11 I once told Varun Sir, in front of everyone, "Why should I? Give me detention, I don't care." He had asked me to read my answer aloud. I remember crossing my arms and staring at the fan while thirty people went "ooooh". What nobody knew was that I'd been up till two every night that week helping at my uncle's dhaba after my father's accident, and I hadn't written any answer at all. Reading aloud would have shown that. Varun Sir didn't write me up. He said, "Stay back after class, Akash." I expected a lecture. Instead he asked, "Is this about the reading, or about something else?" I nearly said nothing again. Then it all came out: the dhaba, the hospital, the no sleep. He moved my deadline and, with my permission, told the school counsellor I needed some flexibility. I stopped backtalking him after that. Not because I was scared. Because he'd asked.

qa.a: The thirty classmates going 'ooooh' likely saw plain rebellion, not the tiredness and fear behind it.
